question.problem:
A shop sells spray foam in small and large cans. The volume of liquid in a small can is normally distributed with a mean of $0.3\,\text{ltrs}$ and a standard deviation of $0.003\,\text{ltrs}.$ The volume of liquid in a large can is normally distributed with a mean of $0.6\,\text{ltrs}$ and a standard deviation of $0.008\,\text{ltrs}.$

The foam from a small can expands $40$ times its liquid volume after being sprayed in place, while the foam from a large can expands to $60$ times its liquid volume. 
If one small and one large can are randomly selected, what is the probability that the total foam volume from both cans after expanding is less than $49\,\text{ltrs}?$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9713\,$ | $\,0.9719\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ | $\,0.9732\,$ | $\,0.9738\,$ |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9772\,$ | $\,0.9778\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ | $\,0.9788\,$ | $\,0.9793\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9821\,$ | $\,0.9826\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ | $\,0.9834\,$ | $\,0.9838\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the volume of liquid in a small can, and let $Y$ denote the volume of liquid in a big can. We want to find 

$$
P(40X+60Y<49).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are  independent random variables such that $X∼N(0.3,{0.003}^{2})$ and $Y∼N(0.6,{0.008}^{2})$, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}40X+60Y & ∼N(40\cdot 0.3+60\cdot 0.6,{40}^{2}\cdot {0.003}^{2}+{60}^{2}\cdot {0.008}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(48,0.2448).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variable $40X+60Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =48$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{0.2448}.$

In order to find $P(40X+60Y<49),$ we convert $40X+60Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(40X+60Y<49) & =P(Z<\frac{49-48}{\sqrt{0.2448}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<2.02) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.02) \\  & =Φ(2.02)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(2.02)≈0.9783.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(40X+60Y<49) & ≈Φ(2.02) \\  & ≈0.9783.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that the probability that, after expanding, the total volume of foam is less than $49$ liters is $0.9783.$
